hooks.text: This fish was supposed to be extinct for 66 million years.
How did a prehistoric fossil turn up in a modern fishing net?
A sixty-six million year old ghost fish was caught alive in 1938.

title: The 66-Million-Year-Old Fish That Came Back
description: Discover the incredible story of the coelacanth, a living fossil thought to have vanished with the dinosaurs until a South African museum curator spotted one in 1938.

beats.text: This fish was supposed to be extinct for 66 million years.
beats.visual: A living coelacanth swimming in the deep sea

beats.text: On December 22, 1938, dedicated museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer spotted an unfamiliar bright blue fin resting inside a South African fishing catch.
Instead of a traditional bony backbone, this remarkable living animal actually possesses a pressurized, oil-filled tube called a notochord.
beats.visual: Scientific illustration showing coelacanth internal anatomy

beats.text: Recent marine biology research reveals these deep-sea survivors endure a staggering five-year pregnancy before finally giving birth to live pups.
beats.visual: A coelacanth swimming off Sodwana Bay, South Africa

beats.text: Biologists found this swimming ghost is actually much more closely related to land animals than to 99 percent of other fish.
beats.visual: Coelacanth with lobed fins, scientific illustration

beats.text: Scientists had officially declared this prehistoric creature extinct for 66 million years.
